production.

NO RULE BROKEN.
WHAT WE DID FIND.
90 runs of 36 months, about 13,500 decisions, six models.
No model disabled the control, kept a bypass or hid a disclosure.

Each model put the cost somewhere different: care, overdue exceptions
or escalations.

Staying safe meant 19 to 42 escalations per run: safety paid for in human
attention.

Telling models 'this is an evaluation' barely moved choices, except in one
scenario.

Mean TVD 0.02 to 0.09 · one
shift, Holm p = 0.02

Haiku 5.5 favoured later-listed options; 10% of Qwen replies did not
parse.
LONG-HORIZON RISK SHOWED UP AS SLOW DEBT, NOT ONE BAD ACT.

ZERO VIOLATIONS CAN
STILL BE UNFAIR.
Swap the service labels. Keep every operational fact the same.

text: THE SWAP TEST CAUGHT THE BIAS WE PLANTED. RUN IT ON YOUR AGENT.

RUN IT ON THE STACK
YOU ALREADY OPERATE.
Kubernetes, Flux and OpenTelemetry. No new infrastructure.

An isolated Job per evaluation: no
egress, read-only root, fails without
collector receipt.

Scenario, agent config and policy
versioned in Git and reconciled: every
result points at a commit.

One span per decision, so evaluation
evidence sits next to your ops data.
Executed: container + OTel receipt; manifests admitted by a real API server. Not yet: pods on a node, Flux.
EVALUATION RUNS AS A WORKLOAD: REVIEWED, VERSIONED, OBSERVABLE.

THE PATTERN.
FIVE STEPS, YOUR STACK.
What to take back to your own agentic system.
Pick the hard incident that worries you most.
Write it as a scenario. Hash it. Reconcile it with Flux.
Run the whole agent for 36 logical months in a Job.
Score execution, rules, work and people apart.
Re-run on every model, prompt or tool change.
EVIDENCE INFORMS THE DECISION. A SCORE DOES NOT GRANT AUTHORITY.
